Tell the scanner what kind of page it is, or let it decide. Each kind has its own fields and a sensible place for the data to go, which you can change before anything is saved.

tree: Faded ink, ruled pages and cramped handwriting are what this was built for. A few habits make every page read cleaner.

tree.style: margin: 24px 0 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; display: grid; gap: 14px;
flex: none; width: 38px; height: 38px; border-radius: 10px; display: grid; place-items: center; background: #f2f9f6;

tree: Daylight or an even lamp keeps faint ink readable.

tree.style: flex: none; width: 38px; height: 38px; border-radius: 10px; display: grid; place-items: center; background: #f2f9f6;

tree: Keep all four corners in view so no column is cut off.

tree.style: flex: none; width: 38px; height: 38px; border-radius: 10px; display: grid; place-items: center; background: #f2f9f6;

tree: For a book, photograph each page; for many pages, a PDF is easiest.

tree.style: display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 0.8fr) minmax(0, 1.2fr); gap: 48px; align-items: start;
margin: 0 0 12px; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: .16em; text-transform: uppercase; font-weight: 600; color: #07784c;
background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: Yes. It is built for handwritten registers, ledgers and price lists as well as printed pages. Anything it is unsure of is marked for you to check.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: JPEG, PNG and WebP photos up to 10 MB, and PDFs up to 20 MB and 40 pages. HEIC photos and Word or Excel files are not supported yet.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: Do I have to say what kind of page it is?
No. You can pick the kind of page, or choose “anything else” and let it sort each row on its own.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: No. Scanned data waits for your review and goes into your records only after you approve it.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: Can I see the original later?
Yes. The original photo or PDF stays with the scan so you can compare it with what was read.

tree.style: margin: 0 auto; max-width: 760px; font-size: 42px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.1; letter-spacing: -0.03em; color: #fff;

tree: Bring the paper in, one photo at a time.
